principles: A check that cannot fail is removed or repaired, never left registered as decoration.
Every repair ships with the exact mutation that previously slipped through, committed failing first.
Real inventory data over synthetic fixtures wherever the check's purpose is the real inventory.
Guards must distinguish legitimate exceptions explicitly (a marker with a reason), never by silently widening.
Persist parsed, bounded evidence; never raw provider output.
drivers: B-a745 F-002 and F-012 and two implementer reports showed four green checks protecting nothing.
B-41c8's REVIEW rounds used commit subjects the current RED guard cannot even see, so the guard's blind spot is already live.
cross_host_review runs are expensive (Codex quota, agy minutes); discarding the independent host's findings wastes them and hides disagreement.
Each item is a different file, so parallel fresh workers keep the story short.

options.name: A-repair-each-check-with-its-mutation
pros: Each check gains a committed failing mutation, so the credibility claim is mechanical.
Four independent files allow parallel implementation.
The RED guard becomes a shared helper reusable by other suites.
cons: Four RED/GREEN pairs and four reviews of small diffs.
The orphan sweep may find more orphans than the two known ones and must classify each.

options.name: B-delete-the-weak-checks
cons: Loses the membership check, the RED guard and cross-host findings entirely; the story's user value is that these checks bite, not that they vanish.

options.name: C-one-generic-test-credibility-framework
pros: A single mutation-testing harness could cover future checks.
cons: Far larger scope, speculative, and would delay the four concrete repairs the evidence already demands.

rationale: Option A is the only one that delivers the story's stated value (four checks that bite) with mechanical proof per item, and the four disjoint files make it cheap to parallelise. Option B discards checks whose intent is still needed. Option C is a framework nobody asked for; the shared RED-guard helper in A captures the reusable part without it.

preMortem.scenario: CHK-001 registers validation-protocol-smoke and it fails on case-insensitive filesystems only.
preMortem.trigger: The CASE_MISMATCH assertion depends on filesystem case sensitivity.
preMortem.consequence: The full suite reddens on macOS but not Linux.
preMortem.mitigation: The RED case must reproduce the failure on this macOS checkout; the GREEN fix must either make the check filesystem-aware or skip with an explicit reason, and the smoke runs in the full suite on this machine before REVIEW.

preMortem.scenario: The real-data membership case flags test:serial-reference-prefix members as stalePolicy and fails on a healthy tree.
preMortem.trigger: The prefix chain is a separate inventory.
preMortem.consequence: A false failure that trains operators to ignore the smoke.
preMortem.mitigation: The case evaluates both chains (test:serial-reference-prefix plus test:serial-reference) against RESOURCE_POLICY and asserts PASS on the real tree before asserting FAIL on the scratch mutation.

preMortem.scenario: The extended RED guard rejects this story's own history or B-41c8's merged history.
preMortem.trigger: Subjects like 'RED: B-41c8 CHK-001 ...' do not match the new regex, or a merge commit carries no marker.
preMortem.mitigation: The guard scans only main..HEAD of the current branch, accepts the documented subject forms (RED(CHK-nnn):, RED(F-nnn):, and the colon form used by B-41c8 if adopted), and the story's own commits follow the format it enforces.
